# 06_check_duplicates_and_zero_bytes.sh - Find duplicate and empty files

<!-- BEGIN pipeline-callers: generated by tools/automation_doc_links.py, do not edit by hand -->
:::{attention} Usually run by a Bitbucket pipeline
`06_check_duplicates_and_zero_bytes.sh` is normally not run on its own. The Bitbucket pipelines listed below call it as one step of a longer job, after earlier steps have prepared its inputs and environment. Run it by hand mainly for debugging or local testing.

## Description

Uses the checksums and sizes from [02_create_manifest.sh](#help-02_create_manifest) to find files with identical content and files with zero bytes. It prints a summary to the log and writes two Markdown reports, which [24_amend_report.sh](#help-24_amend_report) copies into the report.

## Usage

```bash
./automations/06_check_duplicates_and_zero_bytes.sh <directory> [tag] [date]
```

- `directory` - Deposit directory (used in the log summary).
- `tag` - Optional suffix of the manifest files to read.
- `date` - Date stamp of the manifest, `YYYY-MM-DD` (default: today). Pass it when the manifest was created on a different day.

## Inputs and outputs

- Reads `generated/manifest[.tag].<date>.sha256` and `generated/metadata[.tag].txt`
- Writes `generated/duplicate-files-report[.tag].<date>.md` and `generated/zero-byte-files-report[.tag].<date>.md`
- When zero-byte or suspiciously small files are found, the zero-byte report ends with a link to a post on cloud-storage placeholders (Dropbox etc.) and a possible solution.
- Writes `generated/duplicate-files-full[.tag].<date>.md`, the complete list of duplicate files
- Writes `generated/zero-byte-files-full[.tag].<date>.md`, the complete lists of zero-byte and suspiciously small files

The duplicate report in the main body of the report stays short: it gives the number of files checked, the number of files that have a duplicate, and the number of groups of identical files, followed by a sample of at most 12 duplicate files. When there are more, it points to the full list, which [24_amend_report.sh](#help-24_amend_report) puts in the appendix ("Appendix: Duplicate files"). Set the environment variable `DUPLICATES_SAMPLE_LINES` to change the sample size.

The zero-byte report is pruned the same way. It has two sections, each with a count and a sample of at most 12 files, pointing to the full lists in the appendix ("Appendix: Zero-byte and suspiciously small files"):

- **Zero Byte Files**: files with a size of 0 bytes.
- **Suspiciously Small Files**: files of a binary type (Stata, Excel, PDF, ZIP, images, R and MATLAB data, ...) with a size above 0 but below 512 bytes. A real file of these types has a larger header, so such files are typically placeholders left by Dropbox, OneDrive or git-lfs rather than the data itself. Set `SMALL_FILE_BYTES` to change the threshold and `SMALL_FILE_EXTENSIONS` (space-separated, lower case, no dot) to change the list of types. `DUPLICATES_SAMPLE_LINES` sets the sample size for both reports.
